rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card, impostor table and dated predictions before data; real-skeleton synthetic validation (six worlds, null sizes, mover power); replication on 4 periods and 4 natives (G38, G39, G41, G44) in two embedding models and two variants; estimates rows; confirm.py frozen with a passing dry run (not run). Missing: NE19 holdout run, read-out mechanism for movers, field measured as work.
rationale.faithfulness: The endogenous (spontaneous) part is the solid result: rooms differ beyond composition and the measured field directions in 5/7 regime-III periods, both models, with a calibrated null. The explicit-field-as-direction prediction failed, movers are mixed (1 clean adoption, 1 carry, 1 pre-aligned), and the coupling-vs-self-made-drive question is open. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A design fact for operators: separate rooms diverge even with identical instructions, room-specific instructions double the split but not along their text, and nothing persists across goals; moved agents may keep their old project. Computable from logs with an embedding model, but no lever with a predicted effect size.

one_line: The #best/#rest content split is mostly endogenous and regenerates at each goal; room-specific instructions double it but not along their text, composition explains little, and movers split between adopting and carrying.

v2.claim: In regime-III two-room periods, the #best/#rest content separation exceeds random regroupings after removing members' leave-period-out constants and the measured room-field directions (Q_spont > 1, p < 0.05 in 5/7 bge, 4/7 gte; 3/5 identical-kickoff periods in both models; f_comp 0.03-0.18 where rooms separate). The residual is endogenous, not identified as coupling. Excluded: the explicit-field direction (P3 failed), movers (P5 mixed, 5 movers), remanence (a separate negative), the post hoc 'trigger' reading and the fielded-vs-identical ranking (rank p 0.048).
v2.scope: 7 regime-III two-room non-holdout periods (#36-#44), both embedding models; G35 (regime II, no composition removal) is not part of the claim

adjudication.decision: Score the residual-divergence clause as worded by the blind rater, with 'spontaneous' replaced by 'endogenous, not identified as coupling'. Fragile is false. The coordinator's residual objection is kept as one open-impostor penalty (x0.8), not as fragility or a x0.6 penalty.
reasons: Fragile (RUBRIC clarification; rule 5): the flag refers to the scored headline changing sign or significance between data versions or reasonable variants. H100 has one data version, and the headline (a residual split in most regime-III periods) holds in both models (5/7, 4/7) and both vector variants. That #39 and #42 swap between models is partial robustness. An interpretive gap (what fills the residual) is not fragility.

Rule 1: the scored clause is the measured quantity, the residual after composition and measured field directions. That unmeasured work fields can sit in it threatens the word 'spontaneous', not the clause. So the claim is reworded ('endogenous, not identified as coupling') and the gap is carried as an open impostor (x0.8, as in H07's adjudication). The fielded-week ranking (rank p 0.048) is post hoc and an exclusion. It does not lower the identical-kickoff result (3/5 periods in both models; #41 p 0.001).

Rule 8: the coordinator stacked the synthetic (x1.5) and the relabel null (x1.3) from one design. They are credited once as a calibrated null (x2). The mover-power penalty (x0.85) concerns the excluded mover clause and is dropped (rule 1).
Mechanism: M0. The rejected rivals (composition, text-direction field) leave the mechanism open (coupling vs a self-made room drive), so the rater's M1 is not supported.
